summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.

Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Anagarika Munindra. She taught Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, Jack Kornfield, and Sylvia Boorstein.

Dipak Kumar Barua (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. At the University of Calcutta, he was an Assistant Lecturer in Pali from around 1964 and Dean in 1987, later serving as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1996–2004).

Dipak Ranjan Das is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was a lecturer at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and served in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipankar Bhattacharya is an Indologist and linguist who pursued his PhD at National Sanskrit University (2023–2026). In 2025, he served as Project Manager (Content & Research) at Rishihood University.

Dipesh Chakrabarty (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1983–1995) before becoming a professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff (born 1938) is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA and doctorate from Leiden University. He served at Leiden University as a lecturer in 1967 and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.
Dirk Huizinga (1840–1903) studied at the University of Groningen from circa 1858 to 1867 and later held a post there from 1870 to 1901.

Dirk Jan Hoens (1920–2003) was a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, earning a PhD (1951) and Dr.Theol. (1955). He also served as an assistant at Utrecht University from 1948 to 1982.
Dirk Schmidt works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He was a PhD student and teaching assistant at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2022, pursuing his PhD there (attested 2026).

Dirk van Hinloopen Labberton (1874–1961) was an Indologist and linguist who earned doctorates from Leiden and Amsterdam. He taught at Gymnasium Willem III, Bestuursschool, and the University of Tokyo, later serving as teacher and Rector at Theosofisch Lyceum (~1928–1937).

Divya Prakash Pathak works in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned an MA in Sanskrit from Jawaharlal Nehru University (2021–2023) and became a Research Scholar at the University of Delhi in 2023.

Divyaraj Amiya works in Indology and linguistics. He is affiliated with the faculty at the University of Tübingen and serves as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich (both attested 2026).

Diwakar Acharya (born 1969) is an Indologist and philosopher who earned an MA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Kyoto University and became a fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, in 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu around 1882. He later served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from circa 1912 to 1932.

Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij (1853–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Minaev, Jagić, Potebnja, and Bergaigne. He held professorships at Odesa, Kazan, Kharkiv, and Saint Petersburg universities, and became a member of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences in 1907.

Dmitry Aleksandrovich Suleykin (1900–1948) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1920–1925). From 1935 to 1938, he was a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Dmitry Danilov works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mariupol State University, the University of Vienna, Vasyl' Stus Donetsk National University, and was a PhD candidate at the H.S. Skovoroda Institute of Philosophy in 2015.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at Saint Petersburg State University and Berthold Delbrück at the University of Jena. He held posts at Saint Petersburg, the University of Tartu, and Voronezh State University.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
